newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp may acquire more power assets.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp may acquire more power assets.

text.p: PacifiCorp, which confirmed Friday plans to purchase U.K.-based Energy Group, is still looking to acquire electricity generating assets in the U.S., company officials said.

"We plan to continue to build off of our fuel resources and generation, leading on value all the way through to the light switch," Dick O'Brien, PacifiCorp's chief financial officer, said in a conference call with reporters.
He said it was an "open secret" that PacifiCorp was looking at power plant sales by New England Electric System as well as California's Southern California Edison Co and Pacific Gas & Electric Co.
"We see a need to acquire assets, like we tried at Big Rivers," said Dennis Steinberg, PacifiCorp senior vice president.
PacifiCorp is in a court battle, so far at the losing end, over a reorganization plan for Kentucky-based Big Rivers Electric Corp, which will lease back its generating assets.
Such agreements are "the cheapest way to effect control" of power plants, Steinberg said.

PacifiCorp also said it was working with independent power producers in California, which are required to terminate contracts with the state's investor-owned utilities as part of a mandated deregulation plan.

Steinberg said Citizens Power, the power marketing unit acquired by Energy Group last month, has had a leading role in working with the California companies to restructure those "qualifying facility" contracts.
He said such leveraging of customer relationships represents one of the most important benefits of the deal.
PacifiCorp hopes to generate the same type of synergies from Energy Group's Peabody unit, the world's largest private coal producer.
O'Brien said the Peabody assets will benefit PacifiCorp by lowering costs to fuel its 7,000 megawatts of coal-fired generating plants in the western U.S.
In addition, PacifiCorp expects to expand relationships with Peabody's coal customers into the power marketing side.
The combination will also broaden opportunities to export coal, O'Brien said.

Expertise from Energy Group's Eastern Electric, the largest electricity distributor in the U.K. in terms of territory, will aid the Oregon-based utility as it works with large industrial customers in the U.S., he added.

The U.K.'s electricity market will completely open to competition next April, while California will become the first U.S. state to allow competition when it introduces customer choice as of January 1, 1998.
In 1995, PacifiCorp purchased Powercor, an electric distribution and marketing company in the state of Victoria, Australia.
After the Energy Group deal is completed, the Portland, Ore.-based electric utility holding company "will be the first vertically integrated utility on three different continents," O'Brien noted.

He said the $9.6 billion transaction will initially be funded with debt which will be refinanced through the sale of the company's Pacific Telecom unit to Century Telephone Enterprises Inc. for $1.5 billion.
PacifiCorp also plans to sell its Pacific Generation and PacifiCorp Financial Services subsidiaries, company officials said.
"Eventually we will be issuing equity from the utility," said O'Brien, emphasizing that PacifiCorp will seek to maintain the appropriate debt to capital ratio.
((--Deena Beasley, Los Angeles bureau + 1 213 955 6761))
